note: The narration. Each cue is a caption (VTT/SRT) and the on-screen text of the same moment. {repo_url} is filled from config.json. 'screen' says where the text is shown: 'column' = the left text column, otherwise the scene draws it itself.

cues.text:
Which tool?
Which skill?
Which model?
Agents ask a frontier LLM, again and again. Slow and costly.
But the agent's successful runs already hold the answers.
So turn each decision into a table, and train a classifier.
LLM agents read the successful runs and propose features.
They write extraction code, run it in a sandbox, and validate it.
Three judges score each feature. A MetaJudge decides.
Out comes a feature card: one row per candidate.
TabSynth paraphrases the free text to grow the training set.
Candidate and label are copied verbatim, so it never invents a positive.
TabHead, a CatBoost classifier, ranks every candidate in one pass.
Unsure? A confidence gate hands the decision back to the LLM.
Per decision: about 10³× lower latency and 10⁵× lower cost than the GPT-5.4 shortlister.
And it recovers essentially all of the tools the GPT-5.4 shortlister used on its successful runs (Recall@9).
TabAgent: distilling LLM agent components into cheap classifiers.
Onboard your own agent from its logs. {repo_url}
